subject: Deal burn alignment: CloudScale pilot (CS-3472) — weekly sync
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Meyers <alice.meyers@cloudscale.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Oct 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Deal burn & GPU allocation: CloudScale pilot (CS-3472)

Team — quick heads up ahead of this week’s fleet planning call. CloudScale just signaled a plan to go live with the pilot proof-of-concept in mid-November; they want predictable latency for a 2k QPS-ish inference workload during the canary. Sales is proposing a short-term reserved commit for 8 A100s for the pilot window + 2 burst slots for ramp testing.

Attached: CS-3472-MAP.pdf (mutual action plan)

Primary asks:
- Confirm infra lead time if we commit 8 A100-equivalent GPUs starting 2028-11-10.
- Finance: rough committed vs burst cost delta for a 6-week pilot window (estimate).
- Ops: fallback plan if capacity is constrained (we may need to route to hosted fallback).

Can everyone weigh in before tomorrow’s weekly fleet planning (Tuesday 09:00 PT)? I’ll summarize and share the MAP with Alice after alignment.

— Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 02 Oct 2028 10:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal burn & GPU allocation: CloudScale pilot (CS-3472)

Jordan / team — thanks for the heads up. Short summary from infra perspective:

- Lead time: If we allocate from Dedicated pools (reserved), we can stand up the instances in ~11 business days if current capacity is free in the us-west pool. If we need to carve new instances (hardware provisioning), plan is ~6 weeks.
- Practical ask: before committing reserved capacity, we need a 7-day traffic profile and an expected concurrency distribution (p50/p95 p99 latencies target) — CloudScale’s MAP helps but we need QPS-to-GPU mapping.
- Mitigations: we can support the pilot with 4 A100-equivalent reserved + autoscaling burst (2x ephemeral nodes) if the model is quantized to int8 and batching is increased — that reduces steady reserved need and gives CloudScale the SLA-like behavior during peak windows.

Constraints: a competing pilot (deal: ACME-ML) has 6 A100s already scheduled for the same window; we can reassign burst capacity but not guaranteed reserved increases without earlier notice.

I’ll be on the fleet planning call and can share a quick runbook: steps to expedite provisioning, fallback routing (hosted), and a temporary kv-prefix cache suggestion to reduce tokens on hot queries.

— Karthik
Director, Infrastructure

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Oct 2028 09:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal burn & GPU allocation: CloudScale pilot (CS-3472)

Appreciate the clarity, Karthik. Finance view / constraints:

- We need a run-rate delta: committed 8 A100s for 6 weeks vs hybrid (4 committed + burst). Please put numbers into the attached spreadsheet (proposed-runrate-models.xlsx) with: committed price, burst premium, and estimated token/throughput discount from batching/quantization.
- Approval gates: any reserved commit > $75k/month needs VP finance approval; smaller pilots can be signed by me but require a one-off billing schedule.
- Credit corridor: we can offer a 20% pilot credit on the incremental weeks if the deal converts to a 12-month reserved contract within 60 days — that will help close but we need the conversion commitment in writing.

Ask to Jordan / Marissa: get the 7-day traffic projection and the model latency targets (p95) into the Drive link by EOD Friday so infra and finance can finalize numbers for Monday’s exec review.

— Laura
Director, Finance — Enterprise Revenue
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Alice Meyers <alice.meyers@cloudscale.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Oct 2028 14:50:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal burn & GPU allocation: CloudScale pilot (CS-3472)

Looping in a practical operational plan so we can move quickly if CloudScale signs:

1) Short option (recommended): 4 reserved A100s + 2 burst slots starting 2028-11-10, with a canary ramp schedule (week 1: 25% traffic, week 2: 50%, week 3: 100%). This reduces upfront committed cost and stays within the existing us-west pool constraints.
2) If CloudScale insists on 8 reserved GPUs we need signed PO and target start >= 2028-11-20 (hardware carveout / reassignment delays).
3) Rollback: hosted fallback with model-variant downgrade (smaller param count) — 95% feature parity for 2 weeks while infra backfills capacity.

Attached to this thread: short playbook snippet and the MAP link. Alice — would you be able to share a short 7-day QPS export? If not, Jordan can run an internal sim and send conservative numbers.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Meyers <alice.meyers@cloudscale.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deal burn & GPU allocation: CloudScale pilot (CS-3472)

Thanks everyone — quick wrap and action items before Monday exec review: 

- Jordan: produce conservative 7-day QPS/export and p95 targets; upload to Drive (by EOD Fri).
- Karthik: prepare two costed infra options (4R+2B, 8R) with lead times and an ops runbook (by Mon 09:00 PT).
- Laura: finalize pilot credit language and threshold for VP approval, confirm the $75k/month gate.
- Marissa: draft canary ramp schedule and rollback steps; confirm if hosted fallback requires any contract changes.

Alice / procurement@cloudscale.com — expect a short note from me tomorrow with the MAP and a request for a PO if they elect the 8R path. If they prefer the hybrid, we’ll send a 6-week commitment invoice.

Onward — will present the options in the fleet planning meeting and flag any conflicts with ACME-ML’s reserved window.

— Jordan
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
